'''Péter Frankl''' (born 26 March 1953 in [[Kaposvár]], [[Somogy County]], [[Hungary]]) is a [[mathematician]], [[busking|street performer]], columnist and educator, active in Japan.<ref>http://chukou.passnavi.com/parent/special/98-special4?start=1 interview about Peter Frankl</ref> Frankl studied mathematics at [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in [[Budapest]] and submitted his PhD thesis while still an undergraduate. He holds a PhD degree from the [[University Paris Diderot]] as well.  He has lived in Japan since 1988, where he is a well-known personality and often appears in the media. He keeps travelling around Japan performing ([[juggling]] and giving public lectures on various topics).  Frankl won a gold medal at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] in 1971. He has seven joint papers with [[Paul Erdős]],<ref>{{cite web | title = Erdos0 | work = Erdos Number Project | url = http://www.oakland.edu/enp/Erdos0 | accessdate = 27 November 2007 |archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20071102142100/http://www.oakland.edu/enp/Erdos0 <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archivedate = 2 November 2007}}</ref> and eleven joint papers with [[Ronald Graham]].<ref>{{cite web | title = LIST OF PUBLICATIONS OF PETER FRANKL | url =http://www.renyi.hu/~pfrankl/FPpubl.html | accessdate = 15 October 2015}}</ref> His research is in [[combinatorics]], especially in [[extremal combinatorics]]. He is the author of the [[union-closed sets conjecture]].<ref>[http://garden.irmacs.sfu.ca/?q=op/frankls_union_closed_sets_conjecture Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture], the Open Problem Garden.</ref>

==Personality==
Both of his parents were survivors of concentration camps and taught him "The only things you own are in your heart and brain". So he became a mathematician. Frankl often lectures about racial discrimination.<ref>http://blog.livedoor.jp/bbgmgt/archives/2935820.html 在日ユダヤ人論序説－ピーター・フランクルを通して考える「日本」－</ref>

==Adolescence and abilities==
He could multiply two digit numbers when he was four years old.<ref name =clever>{{cite book |title = 頭のよくなる本 |year=1994 |trans-title=A book to be smart |publisher = wave publisher|isbn=4-900528-37-4}}</ref> Frankl speaks 12 languages (Hungarian, English, Russian, Swedish, French, Spanish, Polish, German, Japanese, Chinese, Thai, Korean) and lectured mathematics in many countries in these languages. He has travelled to more than 100 countries.<ref>{{cite book |title = ピーター流外国語習得術 |trans-title=Peter-style foreign language acquisition techniques |publisher = Iwanami Junior Shinsho }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.peterfrankl.com/profile/index.html|title=【プロフィール】ピーター・フランクル &#91;official web site&#93;}}</ref>

==Activities==
Frankl learnt juggling from [[Ronald Graham]]. He and [[Vojtěch Rödl]] solved a $1000 problem of Paul Erdős. [[Zsolt Baranyai]] helped Frankl to get a scholarship in France, where he became a CNRS research fellow.{{citation needed|date=June 2016}}

For 1984 to 1990, Frankl and Akiyama worked hard organizing a Japanese mathematical Olympiad team, and as a consequence the Japanese team is now a regular participant of the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]].<ref>http://www.jikkyo.co.jp/contents/download/1857219556　nakajima sachiko's interview</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.questia.com/newspaper/1P3-3342144041/student-math-prize-named-after-young-genius |title=Student Math Prize Named after Young 'Genius' |access-date=1 January 2016 |archive-date=11 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160111201251/https://www.questia.com/newspaper/1P3-3342144041/student-math-prize-named-after-young-genius |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Since 1998, he is an external member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://mta.hu/koztestuleti_tagok?PersonId=19032|title=MTA Members: Péter Frankl|publisher=[[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]|language=Hungarian|accessdate=14 October 2015}}.</ref>

He authored more than thirty books in Japanese, and with [[László Babai]], he wrote the manuscript of a book on "Linear Algebra Methods in Combinatorics".{{citation needed|date=June 2016}} With Norihide Tokushige he is the coauthor of the book ''[[Extremal Problems For Finite Sets]]'' (American Mathematical Society, 2018).<ref>Reviews of ''Extremal Problems For Finite Sets'':
*{{citation|title=Review|journal=MAA Reviews|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|first=Mark|last=Hunacek|date=October 2018|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/extremal-problems-for-finite-sets}}
*{{citation|title=none|journal=Mathematical Reviews|first=Fred C.|last=Holroyd|mr=3822342}}
*{{citation|title=none|journal=zbMATH|first=M. P.|last=Chaudhary|zbl=1416.05001}}</ref>

==Frankl conjecture==
{{main|Union-closed sets conjecture}}
For any finite union-closed family of finite sets, other than the family consisting only of the empty set, there exists an element that belongs to at least half of the sets in the family.
